Identify the incorrect statement on the linguistic diversity of India:
o: In 1961 census, 1652 languages were listed as mother tongues in India
Kachchi and Sindhi are Indo-European languages
Austric languages are spoken by the tribal groups in Jharkhand
x: India is one of the most linguistically diverse countries in the world. The 1961 Census recorded more than 1600 mother tongues. However, the Dardi language group belongs to the Indo-European family, not the Sino-Tibetan language family.

s: Main language of Dravidians?
x: The Dravidian languages are mainly Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam.

s: Which one of the following languages belongs to the Austric group?
x: Khasi, spoken mainly in Meghalaya, belongs to the Austroasiatic (Austric) language family.

s: With reference to India, the terms 'Halbi, Ho and Kui' pertain to
x: Halbi, also known as Bastari, is an Eastern Indo-Aryan language spoken by various tribes in central India. Ho, a tribal language, is written in the Warang Chiti script and is the mother tongue of nearly a million tribal people in Odisha and Jharkhand. The Kandhas communicate through Kui, a South-Eastern Dravidian language primarily spoken in Odisha and documented in the Odia script. The Kui language was also referred to as the Kuinga language during the historical period. It is closely related to the Gondi and Kuvi languages.

s: The Dravidian races are mainly confined to which of the following parts of India?
x: The Dravidian races are mainly confined to South India. This race is related to the Dravidian language family, which includes Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Telugu, etc. They are also found in central and southeast India.

s: Which one of the following languages belongs to the Austric group?
x: The languages of Austric group (Austro-Asiatic) are Khasi, Santhali, Mundari and Bhumij etc. It is a language spoken by the Indian tribes.

s: Which one of the following is the largest linguistic group of India?
x: The largest linguistic group in India is Indo-Aryan. This is the most important family of Indian languages and comprises of all the principal languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Punjabi, Sindhi, Rajasthani, Assamese, Odiya, Kashmiri, Urdu, and Sanskrit.

s: The Munda language group belongs to which family?
x: Munda languages (Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Savara) belong to the Austro-Asiatic (Austric) family, so Austric is correct.

s: Which of the following is not the language of Bastar region?
x: Gondi, Halbi and Bhatri are spoken in the Bastar region, whereas Sadari is not a Bastar language; the notes do not state this directly.

s: The speakers of major Indian languages belong to how many language families?
x: Indian languages fall into four main families: Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic and Sino-Tibetan, so the answer is Four.

s: The Dardic branch, including Kashmiri, belongs to which language family?
x: Kashmiri belongs to the Dardic branch of the Indo-Aryan family. Dardic is not a Sino-Tibetan branch.

s: Telugu is classified under which branch of the Dravidian language family?
x: Telugu is South-Central Dravidian; Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam are southern, while Kui, Gondi and Kurukh are Central or North Dravidian.

s: The Austro-Asiatic language family in India is represented by which of the following branches?
x: The Austro-Asiatic family includes the Munda branch, with languages such as Santhali and Mundari, and the Mon-Khmer branch, including Khasi.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kui is a Dravidian language associated with the Kandhas of Odisha. Santhali, Khasi and Garo are correctly matched with their respective branches or families.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ho — Dravidian language of Tamil Nadu
x: Halbi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh. Kui is Dravidian, while Ho and Mundari are Austro-Asiatic Munda languages.

s: The presence of Khasi, an Austro-Asiatic language of the Mon-Khmer branch, is considered evidence that the Meghalaya plateau was once part of:
x: Khasi is treated as evidence that the Meghalaya plateau was once part of peninsular India. Its Mon-Khmer affiliation links it with the Austro-Asiatic linguistic zone.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's language-family shares?
o: The older estimate for Indo-Aryan was about 73 per cent
The 2011 estimate for Dravidian was about 19.64 per cent
The 2011 estimate for Indo-Aryan was about 78.05 per cent
The older estimate for Tibeto-Burman was about 20 per cent
x: The older Tibeto-Burman estimate was about 0.85 per cent, not 20 per cent (20 per cent was the older Dravidian figure).

s: Most of the tribal languages of central and eastern India belong to which language family?
x: Most tribal languages of central and eastern India (Jharkhand-Odisha-West Bengal belt: Santhali, Mundari, Ho) are Austric. Dravidian covers only some central tribal pockets (Gondi, Kui, Kurukh); Sino-Tibetan is the language family of the North-East and Himalaya; Indo-Aryan is the family of the north, west and east plains.

s: Which group consists of the scheduled languages with the smallest number of speakers as per Census 2011?
x: Sanskrit, Bodo and Manipuri are the smallest scheduled languages. Hindi, Bengali and Marathi are the three largest; Telugu, Tamil and Kannada are large Dravidian languages; Kashmiri is not among the smallest, and Punjabi and Odia have many speakers.

s: Gor Boli (Lambadi), spoken by the Banjaras, belongs to which language family?
x: Gor Boli or Lambadi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken by Banjaras across several States and has no script of its own.

s: Which of the following about language families is INCORRECT?
o: Sino-Tibetan spreads across China, Tibet, Myanmar and the Himalayas.
Dravidian languages are mainly found in North India.
Austronesian spreads across South-East Asia, the Pacific Islands and Madagascar.
Niger-Congo has the largest number of languages.
x: Dravidian languages are mainly in South India, not North India; the other statements are correct.

s: Romani, the language originally spoken by the Gypsies (Roma), is related to which languages?
x: Romani is related to the Indo-Aryan languages of India.

s: In which parts of India are Austro-Asiatic (Austric) languages mainly spoken?
o: Central and East India and Meghalaya
x: Austro-Asiatic is spoken in central-east India and Meghalaya; Dravidian in the south, Indo-European in the north, west and east, and Sino-Tibetan in the north-east and Himalayas.

s: Which of the following language – family pairs is correctly matched?
x: Bodo is Tibeto-Burman; Santali is Austro-Asiatic, Telugu Dravidian and Marathi Indo-Aryan.

s: In Census 2011, which language overtook Telugu for third place among India's languages?
x: Telugu was third in 2001, but Marathi overtook it in 2011, pushing Telugu to fourth.

s: In which area of Andhra Pradesh is the Koya tribal language mainly spoken?
x: Koya is spoken in the Godavari agency; Savara in the Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills, Kui/Kuvi on the AP-Odisha border hills and Gadaba in the Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency.

s: Which language–tribe–family combination is correctly matched?
x: Sora is the language of the Savara and belongs to the Munda branch of the Austroasiatic family. Koya and Kuvi are Dravidian, while Lambadi is Indo-Aryan.

s: Who created Ol Chiki, the script of Santhali, in 1925?
x: Raghunath Murmu created Ol Chiki in 1925; Santhali entered the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Amendment, 2003.

s: Bodo belongs to which language family?
x: Bodo is a Sino-Tibetan (Tibeto-Burman) language.

s: Which of the following is NOT an Indo-Aryan language?
x: Kurukh is Dravidian (Central/North branch); Kachchhi, Bhili and Konkani are Indo-Aryan.

s: As per Census 2011, the Indo-Aryan family accounts for what share of India's speakers?
x: Indo-Aryan speakers were 78.05% in 2011 (older figure about 73%); Dravidian 19.64%.

s: Kui/Kuvi, spoken by the Kondhs of Odisha, belongs to which language family?
x: Kui/Kuvi is Dravidian; Savara and Ho are Munda (Austro-Asiatic).

s: Halbi, spoken in Bastar, belongs to which language family?
x: Halbi of Bastar, Chhattisgarh, is an Indo-Aryan language.

s: Gondi, a tribal language of central India, belongs to which language family?
x: Gondi, like Kui and Kurukh, belongs to the Central/North branch of the Dravidian family.

s: Nicobarese belongs to which branch of the Austro-Asiatic language family?
x: Khasi and Nicobarese are Mon-Khmer languages of the Austro-Asiatic family; Santhali and Mundari are Munda.

s: What is the official language in Sri Lanka?
x: Sinhala (Simhalam) is the official language of Sri Lanka, along with Tamil.

s: Which language family is the largest by speakers, accounting for approximately 46% of the world population?
x: Indo-European is the largest family by speakers, about 46% of humanity. Niger-Congo has the most languages.

s: The Bantu languages belong to which language family?
x: The Niger-Congo family, spread across Sub-Saharan Africa, includes the Bantu languages.

s: Which language family is the second largest by number of languages, after Niger-Congo?
x: Austronesian has the second-largest number of languages, after Niger-Congo. Sino-Tibetan ranks second by number of speakers, not languages.

s: Which language family is the second largest by number of speakers?
x: Sino-Tibetan is the second largest family by speakers; Cantonese, Tibetan and Burmese are among its major languages.

s: Which of the following language – family pairs is correctly matched?
x: Swahili is Niger-Congo; English is Indo-European, Mandarin Sino-Tibetan and Tamil Dravidian.

s:
Assertion (A): Mandarin Chinese is the most spoken single language.
Reason (R): Mandarin Chinese belongs to the Sino-Tibetan language family.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: belonging to Sino-Tibetan does not explain why Mandarin has the most speakers.

s: Which Indian language, is spoken the most in the world after Hindi?
x: According to Ethnologue 2025, Bengali is the most spoken Indian language in the world after Hindi among the given options. There are a total of 284.3 million users of the Bengali language globally.

s: Hindi speakers formed what share of India's population in Census 2011?
x: Hindi was spoken by 43.6%, followed by Bengali (8.0%).

s: What is Bengali's rank among the world's most spoken languages?
x: Bengali ranks 7th in the world; Hindi is 2nd and Punjabi 10th.

s: According to the 1961 Census, how many mother tongues were listed?
x: The 1961 Census listed 1,652 mother tongues.

s: In Census 2011, the 1,369 rationalised mother tongues were grouped into how many languages?
x: They were grouped into 121 languages: 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled.

s: How many languages and dialects did Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India (1903–1928) record?
x: Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India recorded 179 languages and 544 dialects between 1903 and 1928.

s: For Census language classification, a language generally needs at least how many speakers?
x: The Census counts a language when it has 10,000 or more speakers.

s: In Census 2011, about how many raw mother tongue returns were recorded before rationalisation?
x: About 19,500 raw returns were rationalised to 1,369 mother tongues and grouped into 121 languages.

s: Who led the People's Linguistic Survey of India, which recorded 780+ languages?
x: G.N. Devy led the People's Linguistic Survey; Grierson's survey (1903-1928) recorded 179 languages.

s:
The Constitution (71 st Amendment) Act, 1992, amends the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages?
1. Konkani
2. Manipuri
3. Nepali
4. Maithili
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Option (a) is correct: The Eighth Schedule lists the languages officially recognised by the Government of India. It includes 22 languages, of which 14 were originally listed: Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Oriya (renamed Odiya in 2011), Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu. The Sindhi language was added by the 21 st Amendment Act of 1967. Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali were included by the 71 st Amendment Act of 1992, while Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santali were added by the 92 nd Amendment Act of 2003.

s: Which of the following language is not included in 8th schedule?
x: Rajasthani is not among the 22 Eighth Schedule languages, while Gujarati and Kashmiri (1950) and Dogri (2003) are. Hence Rajasthani is the answer.

s: Which among the following language was added in 8th Schedule of the Indian Constitution in 2003?
x: Santhali was added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003 along with Bodo, Dogri and Maithili. Konkani and Manipuri came in 1992 and Sindhi in 1967.

s: Which three languages have been added to the 8th Schedule of Indian Constitution by 71st Amendment?
x: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali. Sindhi was added earlier in 1967, and Kashmiri and Assamese were original 1950 entries.

s: From the following languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution pick out the one which is official language of a state
Under which one of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts, four languages were added to the languages under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, there by raising their number to 22?
x: The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, taking the Eighth Schedule from 18 to 22 languages.

s: Which one of the following is correct about the languages mentioned in the Constitution of India?
o: State can compel the linguistic minorities to choose their mother tongue as a medium of instruction in primary schools.
‘Angika’ is now included in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution.
Hindi is a national language of India.
Bodo is recognised as language in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution.
x: Bodo was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment (2003). Angika is not listed, Hindi is the official language rather than a national language, and a State cannot compel minorities on medium of instruction.

s: Which language is not included in 8th schedule of Indian Constitution?
x: Bhojpuri is not in the Eighth Schedule, whereas Urdu, Nepali and Konkani are.

s: The 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule cover approximately what percentage of the population's mother tongues?
x: The 22 scheduled languages cover the mother tongues of approximately 96.71 percent of the population.

s: Which languages were added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003?
x: The 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule.

s: The 96th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 changed the name of which language in the Eighth Schedule?
x: The 96th Amendment changed the constitutional name of the language from Oriya to Odia. It did not add a new language to the Eighth Schedule.

s: Which community is associated with the demand for the inclusion of Gor Boli in the Eighth Schedule?
o: Koya community of the North-Eastern region
Banjara or Sugali community of Andhra Pradesh
x: The Gor Boli demand is associated with Andhra Pradesh's Banjara, or Sugali, community.

s: How many languages did the 71st Amendment (1992) add to the Eighth Schedule?
x: The 71st Amendment added three languages: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; it was the 92nd that added four.

s: In which year was the Sitakant Mohapatra Committee on inclusion of languages in the Eighth Schedule constituted?
x: The Sitakant Mohapatra Committee was constituted in 2003 and the Ashok Pahwa Committee in 1996; there are no fixed criteria for inclusion.

s: In which year was Sindhi added to the Eighth Schedule?
x: Sindhi was added in 1967 by the 21st Amendment, the first addition to the Eighth Schedule, raising the total from 14 to 15.

s: With regard to the Eighth Schedule, English has:
x: English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.

s: A language community seeks authoritative translation of the Constitution under Article 394A, interpretation in Parliament and central development funds. These are principally associated with:
o: Recognition as a non-scheduled Census language
Classification as a dialect under Hindi
Recognition by the People's Linguistic Survey alone
x: Interpretation in Parliament, authoritative constitutional translation under Article 394A and central development funds are stated benefits associated with Eighth Schedule inclusion.

s: In which year was the Ashok Pahwa Committee on criteria for the Eighth Schedule set up?
x: The Ashok Pahwa Committee dates to 1996; the Sitakant Mohapatra Committee to 2003.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Eighth Schedule:
1. It originally had 14 languages.
2. The 96th Amendment added Odia as a new language.
3. Sindhi was the first language added, in 1967.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: the Eighth Schedule began with 14 languages in 1950. Statement 3 is correct: Sindhi was the first addition, by the 21st Amendment in 1967. Statement 2 is wrong: the 96th Amendment (2011) only renamed 'Oriya' as Odia and added no new language.

s: Which of the following languages is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule?
x: Bhojpuri, like Kokborok and Gor Boli (Lambadi), is not in the Eighth Schedule; Konkani and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment.

s: By which Constitutional Amendment was Sindhi added to the Eighth Schedule?
x: The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi, the first addition, raising the count to 15.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule?
x: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali, raising the number to 18.

s: Which language was declared a classical language of India in 2014?

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Article 343 – Hindi in Devanagari as official language of the Union
Article 345 – State Legislature adopts the official language(s) of the State
Article 351 – Union's duty to develop Hindi

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Article 350B — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 351 — Union’s duty to develop Hindi
Article 343 — Official language of the Union

s: The Official Languages Act, 1963 is significant because it:
o: Required every State to adopt the three-language formula
Continued the use of English alongside Hindi after 1965
Removed Hindi from the Union’s official-language framework
Made Sanskrit the sole official language of the Union

s: Which Article provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?

s: What does Article 351 of the Constitution deal with?
o: The Union's duty to develop Hindi
x: Article 351 sets the Union's duty to develop Hindi; 344 is the Commission and 345 State languages.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the use of English in the Supreme Court, High Courts and Acts?
x: Article 348 provides for English in the Supreme Court, High Courts and in Acts.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage?
x: Article 350A asks States to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage; 350B is the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for an Official Language Commission appointed by the President?
x: Article 344 provides for the President's Official Language Commission and a Parliamentary Committee.

s: Where was the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, set up under Article 350B in 1957, located?
x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was appointed in 1957 with the office at Allahabad.

s: Hindi Diwas is observed on 14 September to mark the adoption of which of the following?

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Recently, all the countries of the United Nations have adopted the first-ever compact for international migration, the ‘Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM)’.
2. The objectives and commitments stated in the GCM are binding on the UN member countries.
3. The GCM addresses internal migration or internally displaced people also in its objectives and commitments.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration is the first intergovernmental agreement, adopted under the auspices of the United Nations, to cover all dimensions of international migration in a holistically and comprehensive manner. It was adopted at an intergovernmental conference on migration in Marrakesh, Morocco, on 10 December 2018. At the ceremony to adopt the text on 10 December, only 163 countries formally adopted it. Further, countries like Austria were critical of it and refrained from adopting it in 2018. Hence statement 1 is not correct. The Global Compact for Migration is the first-ever UN global agreement on a common approach to international migration in all its dimensions. The global compact is non-legally binding. Hence, statement 2 is not correct. The Global Compact enumerates 23 objectives for State action, bolstered by specific commitments, that seek to address challenges related to today’s migration. The GCM commitments and actions can be seen as a guide for States to meet their human rights obligations when designing migration governance measures to reduce the risks and vulnerabilities migrants face at different stages of migration and to create conducive conditions that empower all migrants to become active members of society. Key commitments include: Strengthening evidence-based and human rights-based policy-making and public discourse on migration; Minimizing the adverse drivers of migration, including combating poverty and discrimination
